driverRegime.method: daily % change of each asset regressed on the daily change in the US 2-year and 10-year yields (basis points) and on the daily % change in WTI; a driver is dominant when |corr| >= 0.4

dataNotes: Run timing: this cycle ran the morning of 16 October 2026 after the GitHub Actions fetch job drafted contracts/*.2026-10-15.json from Thursday 15 October's close. Every figure used is dated at or before the 2026-10-15 close; documents/live.json and news-log entries dated 16 October were NOT used.

Bonds, dollar and IWM sigma are not auto-fetched and were carried stale from the prior board (bonds TLT IV 15, 25 September; dollar EUR/USD 1M IV 4.72, 21 September; IWM RVX 19.97, 23 September). No newer prints were obtained.

News-log entries for 2026-10-15 (five) were confirmed identical to those in the Artifact database; no hand-entered issue entries were dated 15 October. Percentage changes are computed from the drafted 14 and 15 October closes. Cash-index levels and yield moves come from the news log; the news log's CPI/PPI items are used as written (the 14 October board already referenced the CPI print), and PPI/retail-sales actuals beyond the quoted PPI +6.3% y/y were not verified.

No 15 October high-yield OAS, MOVE, breadth count, positioning print, sentiment survey or seasonal statistic was obtained; those category votes are neutral. No separate web search was run (to keep the blindness rule clean), so the news log is the main dated source.

newsLog.event: TSMC posts record Q3 profit but chip and AI stocks fall pre-market
newsLog.numbers: TSMC Q3 revenue $46.72B (+41.2% y/y); net profit NT$763.06B (+68.7% y/y); Q4 revenue guide $52.3B-$54.3B. Pre-market: TSM ~-1.9%, MU ~-4.5%, AMD ~-3%, NVDA ~-2%, ORCL ~-1.8%, CRWV >-6%
newsLog.reaction: Record results failed to lift semis; management was cautious on the 2027 macro outlook and flagged overseas capacity expansion weighing on margins. Nasdaq-100 futures ~-1% pre-market, extending Wednesday's tech rout (Nasdaq Composite -1.9%).
newsLog.tickers: TSM, NVDA, MU, AMD, ORCL, CRWV, QQQ, Nasdaq

newsLog.event: US futures mixed, Nasdaq lags, ahead of PPI, retail sales and jobless claims
newsLog.numbers: Pre-market futures: Dow ~+0.3%, S&P 500 ~-0.2%, Nasdaq-100 ~-1.0%. Wednesday close: S&P 500 -1.0%, Nasdaq -1.9%, Dow -0.1%. 8:30 AM ET data: Sept PPI, retail sales, jobless claims (consensus ~200K vs 197K prior). Sept CPI 3.7% y/y vs 3.6% expected
newsLog.reaction: Hot CPI keeps Fed rate-hike risk in focus (Williams backs one more hike in 2026); tech weakness offsets a steadier Dow. Open hinges on the 8:30 AM ET inflation and consumer data.
newsLog.vsExp: PPI and retail sales actuals not verified at time of logging (n/a)

newsLog.event: September CPI accelerates to 3.7% y/y, PPI jumps 6.3%; Fed rate-hike odds for October spike to near coin-flip
newsLog.numbers: CPI +0.6% m/m, +3.7% y/y (up from 3.4% in Aug); core CPI +0.3% m/m, +2.6% y/y (up from 2.4%). Gasoline +9.1% m/m, record pump price $4.33/gal. PPI +6.3% y/y.
newsLog.reaction: Odds of an October Fed rate hike jumped to near 50/50 from under 25% pre-report; NY Fed's Williams reportedly backs one more 2026 hike. Rate-hike fears hit tech/AI names hardest (Nasdaq-100 -1.3% at the open) while cyclicals outperformed.
newsLog.vsExp: CPI y/y vs 3.6% expected; core m/m vs 0.2% expected; PPI vs 5.5% expected — all hotter than forecast

newsLog.event: S&P 500 closes at 7,746 as Dow jumps ~1% on bank earnings, Nasdaq lags; 10-year yield eases to ~5.09%
newsLog.reaction: Money rotated into cyclicals/financials after bank earnings beats (Dow's financial weighting outpaced the S&P/Nasdaq) and away from AI/large-cap tech following the hot CPI print; Asian tech sold off sharply overnight (Kospi -8%, Nikkei -5%, Taiex -3%) after TSMC's record profit failed to offset margin and 2027-outlook worries.

newsLog.event: US reportedly weighing MOAB strike on Iran's energy and nuclear sites if combat resumes
newsLog.reaction: CNN reports the US has plans to hit Iran's energy infrastructure and nuclear sites with the GBU-43/B MOAB, contingent on Trump ordering renewed combat; analysts question whether it can destroy buried facilities, and Iran's IRGC has threatened US troops and regional data infrastructure in response. WTI eased to $95.21 (+0.1%) and Brent to $104.60 (-1.3%), with oil already pricing in a substantial geopolitical risk premium.
